text:
[IRET.7.10.2] **`latest` modifier** (RLOW.5.6.5). When the
anchor pattern is prefixed with `latest`, the compiler
adds a NOT sub-node immediately after the sequence's last
join, where the anchor and every follower are on the
token. For an anchor at `ts_a` and a first follower at `ts_b`
within window `T`, the NOT node's join test blocks the
match whenever a fact `f` of the anchor's schema has
`ts_a < f.ts < ts_b`, `ts_b − f.ts < T`, and none of the
anchor's `where` and the followers' `where`s, with `f` in
the anchor's place and the followers on the token unchanged,
answers `false` ([RLOW.5.6.5.2], [LTHE.2.5.3], [LNUL.4.7]).

Only the first follower's window and ordering involve `f`: each later
`within` is measured from the step before it ([LTHE.2.3.1]), never from
the anchor. A follower `where` that does not read the anchor already
holds of the token whichever anchor is in place, so the compiler may
omit it from the test. In a two-pattern sequence the last join is the
first follower's.

This reduces the activation set to the single latest
qualifying anchor per match of the followers. `latest` applies only to the
first (anchor) pattern in a sequence; the compiler rejects
it on interior patterns (RLOW.5.6.5.4). The NOT sub-node
is a standard `is_negative = true` beta node; no new node
type is required.

---

idris.name: lthe_2_5_3__chain_later_anchor_does_not_exclude
idris.note: Placed after the sequence's last join and ordering the candidate against the first follower, the sub-node lets a candidate after that follower exclude nothing. Executed.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_3__excludes
idris.note: The sub-node's join test on `ts`: `ts_a < f.ts < ts_b` and `ts_b - f.ts < T`, a standard NOT node's test over the token and one candidate. LESS than the clause: the anchor's `where` and every follower's `where` with `f` in the anchor's place are the fixture lowering's conjuncts in the same test. A substituted `where` that answers `null` blocks the node ([LNUL.4.7]) and excludes under [LTHE.2.5.3] (logical/LTHE.2.5.3_null_candidate_excludes); one that traps blocks the node too, which no clause says.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_3__latest_rules
idris.note: A standard NOT node added after the last join, no new node type. A fixture.

idris.name: rlow_5_6_5_2__window_implied
idris.note: `ts_b - f.ts < T` follows from `ts_a < f.ts` and `ts_b - ts_a < T`: the clause's second condition is implied by its first and the match.
